name: Gold thread lift

lead: Gold thread implantation places very fine strands of gold under the skin, historically in parts of Asia, aiming for tighter skin, fewer wrinkles or a lifting effect on the face. Looksmaxxing discussion of it is sparse.

Proponents describe the threads as stimulating the skin or supporting tissue, and a histopathology study examined skin that had gold threads implanted for facial rejuvenation. One series of 78 patients in Archives of Plastic Surgery looked at gold thread implantation for crow's feet. Most other literature is case reports of threads found on X-rays or CT scans years after treatment.

paras: Threads are inserted under the skin by a practitioner, in cosmetic clinics or acupuncture-style settings. It is sometimes mentioned as an alternative to thread lifts. Gold threads are permanent, so they stay in place after the visible effect has been and gone.

Case reports describe threads migrating, recurrent cellulitis, and incidental findings on imaging that can be mistaken for other conditions or obscure dental imaging. In one fatal case report, gold threads were found at autopsy alongside electroacupuncture injuries; the report attributed the death to pneumothoraces from electroacupuncture, not the threads. Because the threads are permanent, they cannot simply be left to dissolve.

angle.text: Gold threads placed under the skin are promoted for smoother, tighter skin and fewer wrinkles through a skin reaction around the threads. A small series of 78 patients studied it for crow's feet, and case reports describe threads staying in place for years.

lead: Gold thread implantation (also called gold thread therapy or gold thread acupuncture) involves inserting fine gold strands under the skin. Published reports describe it in cosmetic contexts such as facial wrinkles and rejuvenation, and in acupuncture-related contexts such as pain relief. [1][2][3]

The clinical literature is small. A series in Archives of Plastic Surgery evaluated gold thread implantation for periorbital wrinkles in 78 patients. [2] Much of the remaining literature consists of case reports and letters describing radiopaque threads found years later on chest, neck, jaw and spine imaging. [4][5][6][7]
The procedure is mentioned occasionally in looksmaxxing discussions as a 'lift' alternative to thread lifts, but community material is limited and no forum threads are cited here.
infobox: Periorbital wrinkles, facial rejuvenation, pain relief (acupuncture)
Small case series, histology study and case reports

paras: In published case reports, patients describe having gold threads implanted for facial rejuvenation or to relieve neck, back or joint pain, often through clinics offering acupuncture-style treatment. [3][8][9] Gold is radiopaque, so retained threads can appear on X-ray, CT and dental panoramic images. [3][4][10]
A 2012 study in Archives of Plastic Surgery evaluated the efficacy and safety of gold thread implantation for periorbital wrinkles in 78 consecutive patients with mild to severe crow's feet. [2]

A histopathologic and ultrastructural study described the features of gold threads implanted in skin for facial rejuvenation. [11] No randomized controlled trials were identified in the sources reviewed.

A case report describes recurrent cellulitis associated with acupuncture involving migratory gold threads. [8] Reports describe threads in the periorbital region, the whole body, and around the sacroiliac joints in a patient seeking relief for ankylosing spondylitis. [6][5][9]

Radiology reports note that worm-like radiopaque lines from gold threads can be misread as parasites, fractures or ligature wires, and can reduce the diagnostic quality of dental panoramic images. [4][10][12][7]

A forensic case report described a man in his 60s who died after electroacupuncture; imaging showed bilateral pneumothoraces and numerous subcutaneous gold threads. The authors attributed the pneumothoraces to needles penetrating the lung, not to the threads. [1]
